paragraphs.title: The Prohibition against Eating Fat and Blood

easy.question: What was forbidden to eat according to the verse?
answers: Any fat or blood
Only meat
Only bread
easy.explanation: The verse says explicitly, “ye eat neither fat nor blood.”

easy.question: For whom was this statute intended?
answers: The priests only
Your generations
The wilderness generation only
easy.explanation: The verse calls it “a perpetual statute for your generations,” meaning it was intended for future generations.

easy.question: Where was this prohibition to be observed?
answers: Only at the temple
Only in the wilderness
Throughout all your dwellings
easy.explanation: The verse says it applies “throughout all your dwellings,” wherever the people lived.

medium.question: What can be understood from the phrase “a perpetual statute for your generations”?
answers: The prohibition was to continue through the generations
The prohibition was a one-time rule
The prohibition applied to only one generation
medium.explanation: The words “perpetual statute” and “for your generations” show that the command was ongoing.

medium.question: What does “your dwellings” mean in the phrase “throughout all your dwellings”?
answers: Your offerings
The places where you live
Your festivals
medium.explanation: “Your dwellings” refers to the places where the people live, showing that the prohibition applied everywhere.

medium.question: What follows from the wording “neither fat nor blood”?
answers: Blood may be eaten, but fat may not
The prohibition applies only during an offering
Both fat and blood are included in the prohibition
medium.explanation: The phrase names both fat and blood as forbidden foods.

challenge.question: What does the wording “neither fat nor blood” emphasize?
answers: That the prohibition is comprehensive and includes both fat and blood
That only a small amount of fat is forbidden
That the prohibition applies only to the blood of offerings
challenge.explanation: The wording makes clear that both categories—fat and blood—are included in the prohibition.

challenge.question: Why is it important that the verse says “throughout all your dwellings”?
answers: To limit the prohibition to the temple
To clarify that the prohibition does not depend on a particular place
To say that the prohibition applies only in one land
challenge.explanation: The phrase extends the prohibition to every place where the people live, not just a sacred or designated location.

challenge.question: What connection is there between “a perpetual statute” and “for your generations”?
answers: They cancel each other out
One concerns place and the other concerns food
Both reinforce the idea that the command is fixed and continuing
challenge.explanation: “Perpetual statute” indicates permanence, while “for your generations” indicates continuation through future generations.

answers: That the prohibition is comprehensive and includes both fat and blood
That only a small amount of fat is forbidden
That the prohibition applies only to the blood of offerings
questions.explanation: The wording makes clear that both categories—fat and blood—are included in the prohibition.
